day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use the time to travel from the airport to your accommodation in Old Montreal via the 747 express bus (~$11 CAD, budget-friendly). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: After settling in, step outside and explore the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal on foot. Sample iconic Quebec street food including poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and Montreal-style bagels from local vendors and casual eateries along Rue Saint-Paul and Place Jacques-Cartier. Soak in the historic architecture and lively summer atmosphere — no admission fee required.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Old Port waterfront (Vieux-Port) as the sun sets over the St. Lawrence River. Enjoy the free outdoor ambiance, street performers, and public art installations. Pick up a cheap crepe or corn on the cob from a food cart along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and a croissant at a depanneur (corner store) or Tim Hortons near the airport or en route — under $5 CAD.
meals.lunch: First proper meal after arrival: a classic poutine from La Banquise's Old Montreal-area equivalent or a street vendor on Rue Saint-Paul (~$12–15 CAD).
meals.dinner: Marché de la Villette on Rue Saint-Paul — a casual French-style butcher bistro with affordable charcuterie plates and sandwiches (~$15–20 CAD). Alternatively, grab a smoked meat sandwich from a nearby deli.

day_by_day.notes: The 747 express bus from Trudeau Airport to downtown runs 24/7 and costs ~$11 CAD — far cheaper than a taxi (~$50+). Grab an OPUS card at the airport for easy transit use throughout the trip. Old Montreal is very walkable from your hotel, so no transit needed for afternoon/evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro (Orange Line) north to Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest and most vibrant open-air markets. Spend the morning sampling Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, local fruits, artisan breads, and seasonal produce directly from vendors. Many samples are free, and small bites are very affordable. Budget ~$15–20 CAD for tastings and a light market breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mile End neighbourhood on foot, a short walk from Jean-Talon. Visit the famous St-Viateur Bagel shop (open 24/7) for a fresh wood-fired bagel (~$2 CAD). Browse the colourful murals, independent boutiques, and multicultural street life along Rue Bernard and Avenue du Parc. This is one of Montreal's most culturally rich and free-to-explore neighbourhoods.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Festival Crawl: Head down to 'The Main' (Boulevard Saint-Laurent) in the evening, where summer street festivals and pop-up food events come alive. Enjoy live music, local food stalls, and the buzzing nightlife atmosphere. Many events are free to enter. Grab food from street vendors and enjoy the outdoor festival energy.

meals.breakfast: Fresh market breakfast at Jean-Talon — a buttered baguette, local fruit, and a coffee from a market vendor (~$8–10 CAD).
meals.lunch: St-Viateur Bagel with cream cheese and smoked salmon in Mile End (~$8–10 CAD). Eat it on a bench in nearby Parc Sir-Wilfrid-Laurier for a perfect budget picnic.
meals.dinner: Street food along St-Laurent Boulevard during the festival crawl — tacos, grilled corn, or a poutine from a pop-up stall (~$12–15 CAD). Wash it down with a local craft beer from a festival vendor (~$7–9 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Metro fare is ~$3.75 CAD per ride with an OPUS card. Jean-Talon Market is busiest and most lively on weekday mornings — great for authentic local interaction. Check the City of Montreal events calendar (montreal.ca) the night before to confirm any specific St-Laurent festival events happening on this date in July 2027.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (Summer Edition): Check the festival schedule for any daytime gastronomy or arts programming. Many summer festival events in Montreal are free or low-cost. Start the morning by visiting the festival hub area (typically around Place des Arts or the Quartier des Spectacles), exploring free outdoor installations, cooking demonstrations, and cultural performances.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood on foot or by BIXI bike-share (~$3.50 CAD per 30-min ride). Walk up to Mont Royal Park — Montreal's beloved urban mountain — for panoramic views of the city skyline from the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout. The park is completely free. Pack a picnic lunch from a nearby dépanneur to enjoy at the summit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for evening festival programming. Friday evenings in July in Montreal are electric — expect live outdoor concerts, food trucks, and cultural performances, many of which are free. This is the heart of Montreal's summer festival season, and the energy is unmatched.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico in Mile End or a local café near your hotel — classic Montreal café au lait and a toasted bagel (~$7–9 CAD).
meals.lunch: Picnic on Mont Royal: grab supplies from a nearby dépanneur or Marché Atwater — local cheese, crackers, fruit, and a cold drink (~$10–12 CAD total).
meals.dinner: Food truck dinner at the Quartier des Spectacles festival zone — Montreal has an excellent food truck culture in summer. Options range from gourmet grilled cheese to Haitian dishes to smoked brisket (~$12–16 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: BIXI bike-share is one of the best budget ways to get around Montreal in summer. A single-day pass costs ~$8 CAD for unlimited 30-min rides. Mont Royal Park is a 20–25 min bike ride from Old Montreal. Wear comfortable shoes. Check the exact Montreal en Lumière or any overlapping July festival schedule (e.g., Just for Laughs, Festival International de Jazz) closer to the travel date, as summer 2027 programming may vary.

day_by_day.morning: Marché Atwater visit: Head to the beautiful Atwater Market along the Lachine Canal for a final morning market experience. Browse local vendors selling Quebec produce, artisan goods, and prepared foods. Saturday mornings are particularly lively. Pick up affordable local honey, maple taffy, or a fresh pastry as an edible souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or cycle along the Lachine Canal (free, scenic, flat path) back toward Old Montreal. Stop at the Pointe-à-Callière Archaeology Museum if budget allows (admission ~$22 CAD), or enjoy the free outdoor archaeological site and canal-side scenery at no cost. Return to Old Montreal for a final wander through Place d'Armes and Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free to view from outside).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Old Montreal: Enjoy a leisurely dinner in the neighbourhood and take a last stroll along the Old Port. If there are any free outdoor concerts or cultural events happening in Place Jacques-Cartier (very common on summer Saturday evenings), catch a performance under the open sky as a perfect send-off.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry and café au lait from a vendor at Marché Atwater (~$7–9 CAD).
meals.lunch: Classic Montreal smoked meat sandwich at a casual deli near the Lachine Canal or back in Old Montreal — try a local spot rather than a tourist trap on Rue Crescent (~$12–15 CAD).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a budget-friendly BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant in Old Montreal or the Plateau — Montreal is famous for affordable BYOB dining. Pick up a bottle of wine at the SAQ (~$12–15 CAD) and enjoy a full meal for ~$20–25 CAD per person at a local bistro.

day_by_day.notes: BYOB restaurants (apportez votre vin / AVV) are a uniquely Montreal institution and one of the best ways to enjoy a quality meal on a budget. Look for 'AVV' signs in restaurant windows. Saturday at Marché Atwater is peak time — arrive before 10:00 AM for the best selection and fewer crowds. The Lachine Canal cycling path is completely flat and family-friendly, and BIXI bikes are available right at the market.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Old Montreal Stay (~30 min by taxi or express bus 747). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the Vieux-Montréal neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: After settling in, step right outside your hotel door and explore the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Sample classic Québécois street food including poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and Montreal-style bagels. Stroll along Rue Saint-Paul, admire the Basilique Notre-Dame exterior, and soak in the historic port atmosphere. The walk covers roughly 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Old Port waterfront (Quai de l'Horloge area) for sunset views over the St. Lawrence River. Check local listings for any pop-up festival events or outdoor live music happening along the waterfront — summer in Montreal almost always has something going on.

meals.lunch: Grab a classic smoked meat sandwich at a deli on Rue Notre-Dame or a quick poutine from a street vendor during your Old Montreal walk (~$15–20 CAD)
meals.dinner: Garde Manger (453 Rue Saint-François-Xavier) — a beloved Old Montreal bistro with locally sourced Québécois cuisine. Mid-range pricing, lively atmosphere. Budget ~$45–60 CAD per person with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: July 15 falls mid-summer — expect warm weather (~25°C). Light rain is possible but unlikely on any given day given the monthly average of 30mm. Pack a light rain jacket. Old Montreal is extremely walkable from your accommodation, making the afternoon and evening activities easy to reach on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel & Brunch Neighborhood Tour: Take a ~20-minute metro ride (Orange Line to Laurier or bus) to the bohemian Mile End neighborhood. Start at the legendary Fairmount Bagel Bakery (74 Avenue Fairmount O) — wood-fired, open 24/7, and an absolute Montreal institution. Then visit rival St-Viateur Bagel (263 Rue Saint-Viateur O) for a taste comparison. Explore the artsy streets lined with murals and indie boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: St-Laurent Boulevard Festival Crawl: Walk south down 'The Main' (Boulevard Saint-Laurent) from Mile End toward the Plateau. This iconic street hosts numerous summer street festivals and pop-up food events throughout July. Look for the Just for Laughs (Just pour Rires) festival footprint, outdoor patios, and food stalls. Browse local shops, grab a snack, and enjoy the vibrant multicultural energy of one of Montreal's most famous streets.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a live outdoor performance or festival event in the Quartier des Spectacles (a short metro ride or 25-min walk from The Main). In mid-July, the Montreal International Jazz Festival or Just for Laughs Festival may still be running — check schedules in advance. Enjoy the festive atmosphere and street performers.

meals.breakfast: Fresh wood-fired bagel with cream cheese and lox from Fairmount or St-Viateur Bagel (~$6–10 CAD) — the quintessential Montreal breakfast
meals.lunch: Grab street food or a casual bite along St-Laurent Blvd — try Schwartz's Deli (3895 Boul. Saint-Laurent) for a world-famous smoked meat sandwich (~$15–20 CAD)
meals.dinner: Damas Restaurant (1201 Avenue Van Horne, Mile End) — acclaimed Syrian-Mediterranean cuisine with a warm, festive atmosphere. Mid-range at ~$40–55 CAD per person, or opt for a more casual BYOW (Bring Your Own Wine) spot on The Main for ~$30–40 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: July is peak festival season in Montreal — confirm which festivals are active on this specific date at tourisme-montreal.org. The metro Orange Line connects Old Montreal to Mile End efficiently. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for a full day on The Main.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the Orange Line metro to Jean-Talon station and spend the morning at one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air public markets. Sample Quebec artisan cheeses, fresh maple products, seasonal berries, charcuterie, and local produce. Chat with vendors, pick up picnic supplies, and explore the surrounding Little Italy neighborhood streets. Arrive by 9:00–9:30 AM for the best atmosphere before the midday crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (Summer Edition): While this festival is primarily known as a winter event, its summer programming and gastronomy-focused spin-off events often run in July. Check for any scheduled tastings, chef demonstrations, or arts performances in the Quartier des Spectacles or Place des Arts area. If no summer edition is running, visit the nearby Plateau-Mont-Royal neighborhood — explore Parc La Fontaine (a beautiful urban park perfect for a warm afternoon) and browse local boutiques on Rue Mont-Royal.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Montreal for a relaxed Friday evening. The waterfront and Place Jacques-Cartier come alive on summer Friday nights with street performers, outdoor patios, and a festive local crowd. Enjoy the warm evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and a fresh pastry from a café near your Old Montreal hotel before heading to Jean-Talon (~$8–12 CAD)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch assembled from Jean-Talon Market — local cheese, bread, charcuterie, and seasonal fruit (~$20–25 CAD total, excellent value)
meals.dinner: Le Serpent (257 Rue Prince, Old Montreal) — an Italian-inspired restaurant in a stunning industrial-chic space in the Griffintown/Old Montreal border. Known for handmade pasta and local ingredients. ~$45–60 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest on weekends — visiting on Friday morning is a sweet spot for good selection with manageable crowds. Bring a reusable bag for market purchases. Check montrealeenlumiere.com for any summer programming updates well in advance of your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mount Royal Park (Parc du Mont-Royal): Take a taxi or bus to the base of Mount Royal and hike or walk up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a panoramic view of the entire city — a must-do Montreal experience. The park was designed by Frederick Law Olmsted (of Central Park fame). Enjoy the warm summer morning among locals jogging, cycling, and relaxing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Plateau-Mont-Royal or Rue Mont-Royal area for a final afternoon of local exploration. Browse the eclectic vintage shops, independent bookstores, and local boutiques on Rue Mont-Royal Est. If you missed any festival action earlier in the trip, Saturday afternoons on The Main or in the Quartier des Spectacles often feature the most vibrant outdoor programming of the week.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner back in Old Montreal — a leisurely send-off meal celebrating the trip. After dinner, take one last walk along the illuminated cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal and the Old Port, which are especially magical on summer Saturday evenings.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at L'Express (3927 Rue Saint-Denis, Plateau) — a Montreal classic French bistro open since 1980, beloved by locals. Try the eggs Benedict or croque-monsieur. ~$20–30 CAD
meals.lunch: Casual poutine or a crêpe from a Rue Mont-Royal street vendor or quick-service café (~$12–18 CAD)
meals.dinner: Maison Boulud (1228 Sherbrooke St W, in the Ritz-Carlton) for a splurge-worthy farewell dinner featuring refined French-Québécois cuisine — a special treat within a mid-range trip budget (~$70–90 CAD per person). Alternatively, for a more casual but equally memorable option, try Liverpool House (2501 Rue Notre-Dame O) — a Frédéric Morin and David McMillan gem (~$50–65 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the best day to experience Montreal's full energy — markets, festivals, street life, and patios are all at peak vibrancy. If departing on July 19, ensure your final evening allows time to pack and rest. Mount Royal Park is free to enter. Consider renting a BIXI bike (Montreal's public bike share) for the afternoon — it's affordable (~$7–10 CAD for a day pass) and a very local way to get around.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight AC lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Upon landing at Montréal-Trudeau International Airport, arrange a pre-booked luxury private transfer (black car service) to your Old Montreal hotel. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll along the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: Join a guided premium walking tour through the historic cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Sample iconic Québécois street food including artisan poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and wood-fired Montreal bagels. Explore Place Jacques-Cartier, the Old Port waterfront, and the stunning Notre-Dame Basilica exterior while soaking in 400 years of history with an expert local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Garde Manger: Head to this legendary Old Montreal restaurant by celebrity chef Chuck Hughes, celebrated for its indulgent seafood towers, bold Québécois flavors, and lively atmosphere. Reserve well in advance. After dinner, take a romantic evening walk along the illuminated Old Port waterfront promenade with views of the St. Lawrence River.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or a light snack at the airport's Première Classe lounge upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light charcuterie and cheese tasting during the Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk — artisan local products from curated vendors.
meals.dinner: Garde Manger (Old Montreal) — upscale Québécois comfort cuisine; try the seafood tower and foie gras poutine. Budget ~$120–$160 CAD per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Given the 13:00 arrival, keep Day 1 relaxed. Pre-book your private airport transfer and confirm hotel early check-in if possible. The Old Montreal walking tour typically departs in the early afternoon — book a 3:00 PM slot to allow comfortable arrival time. Weather should be warm (~25°C), perfect for outdoor strolling.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel & Brunch Neighborhood Tour: Start the day with an immersive guided tour of the legendary Mile End neighborhood. Visit both St-Viateur and Fairmount bagel bakeries — both wood-fired and open 24/7 — to taste and compare Montreal's most iconic food. Explore the vibrant street art, boutiques, and Jewish and French-Canadian cultural layers of this beloved district with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Travel to the Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets. Join a premium guided food tour sampling aged Québec cheeses, artisan maple products, heirloom produce, fresh charcuterie, and local specialties. Meet passionate producers and learn about Québec's extraordinary culinary terroir. Browse specialty food stalls and pick up gourmet provisions.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Festival Crawl: As evening falls, head to 'The Main' — the iconic St-Laurent Boulevard — where summer street festivals and pop-up food events come alive. Enjoy live music, local craft beverages, and diverse food stalls representing Montreal's multicultural energy. Cap the night with cocktails at a rooftop bar or a craft cocktail lounge along the boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Fresh wood-fired bagels with house-made cream cheese and smoked salmon, enjoyed at Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur as part of the Mile End tour.
meals.lunch: Gourmet tasting lunch at Jean-Talon Market — curated cheese boards, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and artisan breads paired with local ciders or natural wines.
meals.dinner: Monarque (Downtown/Old Montreal border) — an elegant brasserie with a stunning interior, celebrating Québécois ingredients with French technique. Try the duck confit or whole roasted fish. ~$100–$140 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest and most vibrant on Thursday mornings/afternoons — ideal timing. Wear comfortable walking shoes as this is a high-step-count day. The St-Laurent Festival Crawl is best experienced after 6:00 PM when vendors and performers are in full swing. Consider a rideshare or taxi between Mile End and Jean-Talon as they are a short distance apart.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (Morning Events): Immerse yourself in one of Montreal's premier seasonal festivals celebrating gastronomy and the arts. Attend morning programming which may include exclusive chef demonstrations, artisan food market activations, and cultural performances. Check the official festival schedule for 2027 highlights and pre-book any ticketed chef's table or tasting events well in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Cooking Class or Exclusive Chef's Table Experience: Book a premium private Québécois cooking class with a renowned local chef, learning to prepare classics like tourtière, maple-glazed duck, or pea soup elevated to fine dining. Alternatively, secure a coveted afternoon chef's table reservation at a top Montreal restaurant for a behind-the-scenes culinary experience. Return to the hotel for a rest before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière Festival Gala Dinner & Evening Festivities: Experience the festival's signature evening events — often featuring internationally acclaimed guest chefs, outdoor concerts, and illuminated art installations across the city. Attend a festival gala dinner or a special prix-fixe collaboration dinner at a participating top-tier restaurant. Stroll the festival grounds to enjoy live entertainment under the warm summer sky.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Old Montreal property — opt for the full à la carte service with fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, Québec yogurt, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Festival market lunch — graze through the Montreal en Lumière food village sampling dishes from acclaimed local and visiting chefs; budget ~$60–$80 CAD for a curated tasting experience.
meals.dinner: Festival Gala or participating restaurant prix-fixe dinner — expect a 5–7 course tasting menu with wine pairings. Top picks include Toqué! or Le Mousso if participating in festival programming. ~$200–$300 CAD per person with pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Montreal en Lumière festival dates and programming for 2027 should be confirmed and booked as early as possible — gala dinners and chef's table events sell out months in advance. Friday evening will be especially lively with locals and visitors alike. The warm summer weather (~25°C) makes outdoor festival events particularly enjoyable. Keep an umbrella handy given the month's average rainfall.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Old Montreal Morning & Atwater Market Visit: Begin with a slow, luxurious morning — sleep in, enjoy a long hotel breakfast, then take a private guided tour of the Old Port and Atwater Market, Montreal's other beloved public market. Sample artisan cheeses, fresh pastries, local honey, and seasonal produce. Browse the beautiful flower stalls and gourmet food shops at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mount Royal Park & Belvedere Lookout: Take a chauffeured drive or scenic walk up to Mount Royal Park, the iconic hill at the heart of Montreal designed by Frederick Law Olmsted. Enjoy sweeping panoramic views of the city skyline and the St. Lawrence River from the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout. Pack a gourmet picnic assembled from your morning market visit. Optionally visit the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts for a curated cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner at Toqué!: End your premium Montreal journey with dinner at Toqué!, widely considered the city's most prestigious restaurant and a pillar of modern Québécois fine dining since 1993. Chef Normand Laprise's legendary tasting menu showcases the finest seasonal local ingredients with extraordinary precision and creativity. This is a bucket-list dining experience. After dinner, take a final evening stroll through the illuminated cobblestone streets of Old Montreal to savour your last moments in the city.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast — full à la carte with eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh-pressed juices, and artisan pastries.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on Mount Royal assembled from Atwater Market finds — aged Québec cheeses, cured meats, fresh baguette, seasonal fruit, and local sparkling cider.
meals.dinner: Toqué! (Downtown Montreal) — the definitive Québécois fine dining experience. Multi-course tasting menu with optional wine pairings. Reserve 2–3 months in advance. ~$250–$350 CAD per person with pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday at Atwater Market is vibrant and festive — arrive by 9:00–10:00 AM for the best selection before crowds peak. Mount Royal is a 15–20 minute walk or short drive from Old Montreal. If departing on July 19, confirm hotel checkout time and arrange a luxury private transfer to the airport in advance. Toqué! requires reservations well ahead — book immediately upon confirming your trip. This is a perfect celebratory final evening.
